ai.summary: In September–October, 87% of 23 surveyed market contacts cited AI as a salient financial-stability risk, versus 50% of 20 contacts in the spring survey. These are respondents’ views, not a probability of crisis or the Federal Reserve Board’s own risk ranking.
ai.title: Federal Reserve survey puts AI at the top of financial-stability concerns

ai.summary: TechCrunch reported that a petition seeking Jensen Huang’s reinstatement had exceeded 115,000 signatures by Saturday afternoon.
ai.title: Petition seeks Huang’s reinstatement

ai.summary: Meituan’s MIT-licensed multimodal agent model has 1.6 trillion total parameters, with about 48 billion active per token. The company describes long-sequence training and fine-tuning on domestic AI accelerators; this is a vendor engineering report, not independent proof of general hardware or commercial advantage.
ai.title: Meituan releases LongCat-2.5 and describes domestic-accelerator training

ai.summary: Runway made Praxis-1’s weights and inference and fine-tuning code available under Apache 2.0. The company reports partner use on several robot types and benchmark results; these do not establish deployment-wide reliability or economic gains.
ai.title: Runway releases Praxis-1 robot-control model under Apache 2.0

quantum.source: npj Quantum Information; authors’ March 17 preprint
quantum.summary: The authors report a CMOS RF multiplexer at 10 millikelvin with 200 pW static power consumption, readout and flux multiplexing, and XY drive multiplexing in principle. The November journal publication follows a March 17 preprint. Static device power is not total quantum-system energy use.
quantum.title: Cryogenic multiplexer targets quantum-control wiring bottleneck

quantum.summary: Commerce finalized an award of up to $100 million for neutral-atom quantum-computing R&D, including technology to control and validate tens of thousands of qubits. This is research funding for development goals, not a demonstrated fault-tolerant system or commercial advantage.
quantum.title: Commerce finalizes up-to-$100M Atom Computing R&D award

quantum.summary: RIKEN researchers reported a simulated method that reduces physical-qubit and gate requirements for preparing states in a quantum error-correcting code, while maintaining similar simulated logical-operation error rates. The result is a circuit-design study, not a hardware demonstration.
quantum.title: RIKEN proposes fewer steps to prepare protected quantum bits

quantum.summary: The revised preprint reports dielectric-loss protection in a superconducting qubit, with a measured lifetime of 70 microseconds. The greater-than-10-millisecond figure is the inferred dielectric-loss limit, not measured overall lifetime; flux noise remains limiting. First preprint: March 13; revision: November 12.
quantum.title: Parity-protected qubit experiment remains limited by flux noise

editorialReview.note: Seven headline records corrected to originating sources and source dates. Original feed retained in Git history. RIKEN remains attributed secondary coverage of simulations; no raw candidate was promoted.
